login.subtitle: Sign in to manage the synchronization.

pitch.title: Shared iCloud calendars, visible in Google
pitch.body: This app reads iCloud calendars that were privately shared with you and copies their events into a separate Google calendar each – in one direction only.
pitch.point1: The iCloud calendars are never modified.
pitch.point2: Changes go into separate Google calendars, not your main calendar.
pitch.point3: Deletion protection prevents many events from disappearing by accident.

prerequisites.title: These prerequisites must be met:
prerequisites.accepted: The invitation to the shared calendar was accepted on the iPhone (or Mac) with exactly this Apple ID.
prerequisites.web: The calendar is visible in Calendar on icloud.com when you sign in there with this Apple ID.
prerequisites.sameAccount: The app-specific password belongs to the same Apple ID that accepted the invitation.
prerequisites.wait: After accepting, it can take a few minutes until iCloud exposes the calendar. Then run the diagnostics again.
prerequisites.noPublic: Making the calendar public is neither needed nor recommended – the app works only with the private share.

google.title: Google
google.description: Connection to Google and the calendars the events are written to.

connection.title: Connection
connection.intro: Sign in with Google and allow the app to create and fill its own calendar. It has no write access to your other calendars.
connection.accessBasic: Only calendars created by the app
connection.footer: You’ll be sent to Google and brought back here afterwards.
connection.serverMissingTitle: Google isn’t set up on the server

disconnectConfirm.title: Disconnect from Google?
disconnectConfirm.body: The permission is revoked at Google and deleted here. Syncing stops, and after reconnecting you assign the target calendars again. The Google calendars and their events are kept.

extended.title: Extended access (optional)
extended.body: Only needed if you want to use an existing calendar of your own as the target instead of a new one.
extended.point1: The app may then edit events in your own calendars – it only does so in the assigned target calendars.
extended.point2: For a new calendar created by the app, the normal connection is enough.
extended.footer: You can revoke access at any time in your Google Account under “Security”.

calendars.title: Your Google calendars
calendars.footer: Which iCloud calendar writes into which Google calendar is set under “Target calendars”.

primary.title: Use the primary calendar as target?
primary.body1: Synced events are then written right between your own events. Events deleted in iCloud are deleted there too.
primary.body2: A separate calendar is recommended – it can be shown, hidden or removed with one click.

grouping.title: Where does the calendar appear?
grouping.body: Google groups calendars itself: additional calendars you own appear under “My calendars”. The app never shares the target calendars with anyone.

targets.title: Target calendars
targets.footer: Every iCloud calendar writes into a Google calendar of its own. A Google calendar always belongs to one iCloud calendar only.
